title: Random alteration and difference-configuration rank bounds produce sub-n^c difference sets with quadratic local distinct-difference requirements
difficulty: The proof classifies every local equal-difference configuration by projected solution-space dimensions and removes all heavy configurations from a random subset of a progression-free set. It proves a rank-dependent lower bound for distinct positive differences using a technical certification lemma for linearly independent difference equalities. Minimal linear dependencies are decomposed into overlapping components whose variable counts control every implied repetition, closing the local-property construction.

title: Finite metric spaces with rationally independent edge lengths are determined up to isometry by their magnitude functions
difficulty: The proof extracts generalized-series exponents and coefficients from large-scale magnitude asymptotics, then recovers the primitive edge lengths from the resulting additive monoid. Rational independence separates three-edge walk types through their coefficients. A constructive triangle/open-path reconstruction identifies edge incidence and all metric distances despite the initial loss of vertex labels.

title: The basic SDP decides an ordinary finite-domain promise CSP exactly when the orthogonal-vector SDP minion maps to its polymorphisms
difficulty: The argument models arbitrarily large finite-dimensional SDP solutions by finitely supported orthogonal-vector families with compatible minor operations. It proves equivalence of traditional local distributions and clause-vector decompositions by Gram-matrix alignment across connected components. A free-template construction and finite-color compactness then convert exact SDP feasibility into a global minion homomorphism, while evaluation of that homomorphism yields satisfying weak assignments.
